item.title: Turi slams lawyers misleading settlers
item.description: Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD Central Commander Benjamin Turi has condemned lawyers representing illegal settlers, accusing them of knowingly pursuing unwinnable cases and misleading clients into believing they have a chance of success. He said most of the disputed land is either state owned or held by private companies, yet settlers continue to occupy it while claiming legitimacy.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD Central Commander Benjamin Turi has condemned lawyers representing illegal settlers, accusing them of knowingly pursuing unwinnable cases and misleading clients into believing they have a chance of success.

He said most of the disputed land is either state owned or held by private companies, yet settlers continue to occupy it while claiming legitimacy.

Turi accused certain lawyers of exploiting this ignorance for financial gain, dragging cases through the courts despite knowing they will fail.

“It is the lawyer’s responsibility to be honest and inform their clients that the land does not belong to them. Why fool poor settlers until they run out of money and end up homeless?” ACP Turi said.

He said such actions waste police resources, frustrate the courts, and prolong disputes that should have been resolved from the start.

Turi also referenced the recent directive from the National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] instructing squatters to vacate NBC land, stressing that the land belongs to NBC and illegal occupants have no legal standing.

“My advice to the people illegally occupying NBC land is to simply move out. Don’t try to challenge this in court, you will be fooled like other settlers misled by certain lawyers. The land belongs to NBC, and police will move in to evict people forcefully once the court order is served,” he said.

item.title: Daki breaks silence on K200m SME allegations, welcomes audit
item.description: Tambul-Nebilyer MP and former Commerce and Industry Minister Win Bakri Daki has broken his silence on allegations surrounding the government's K200 million Small to Medium Enterprise [SME] stimulus policy, welcoming an audit and insisting it will clear his name. Speaking before a large crowd at his home district in Upper Nebilyer last week, Daki dismissed claims that he misused K200 million in SME
item.content:encoded:
Tambul-Nebilyer MP and former Commerce and Industry Minister Win Bakri Daki has broken his silence on allegations surrounding the government's K200 million Small to Medium Enterprise [SME] stimulus policy, welcoming an audit and insisting it will clear his name.

Speaking before a large crowd at his home district in Upper Nebilyer last week, Daki dismissed claims that he misused K200 million in SME funds, saying the allegations are false and politically motivated.

He explained that the K200 million SME stimulus package is a government policy initiative, similar to the Free Education Policy and the Connect PNG Program, and not a one-off cash allocation placed under the control of the Minister for Commerce and Industry.

Daki said that during his three years as Commerce and Industry Minister, funding under the SME stimulus policy was released progressively and not as a full K200 million package at one time.

"The K200 million SME money doesn't come in full into the Commerce Department. However, K100 million is given to BSP, K70 million to NDB, and the rest comes to Commerce but not in full too," Daki clarified.

He said he fully supports the government's decision to conduct an audit, adding that the process will strengthen the credibility of the department and prove that no funds were misused under his leadership.

Addressing the gathering in the presence of Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa, Provincial Administrator Joseph Mangbil, Tambul-Nebilyer DDA members, community leaders, ward members, and hundreds of suppurters, Daki apologised to the people of Western Highlands for the controversy created by the allegations.

"I am not a thief," Daki told the crowd, maintaining that the accusations were intended to damage his political career.

Despite the allegations, the former Commerce minister received a strong reception from his constituents, with a large turnout of people gathering to hear his explanation, reflecting continued support from many in the electorate.

The allegations are expected to be examined through the government's planned audit, which Daki says he believes will establish the facts.

item.title: Rotary club donates desks to new Alotau primary school
item.description: The Rotary Club of Boroko has donated classroom desks to a newly established primary school in Milne Bay to help students study in a proper learning environment. Gamadoudou Primary School, a newly established Kwato Agency school situated in the western part of Alotau, becomes the fourth school in the province to receive infrastructure support from the club over the past six months.
item.content:encoded:
The Rotary Club of Boroko has donated classroom desks to a newly established primary school in Milne Bay to help students study in a proper learning environment.

Gamadoudou Primary School, a newly established Kwato Agency school situated in the western part of Alotau, becomes the fourth school in the province to receive infrastructure support from the club over the past six months.

Rotary Club of Boroko member, past president, and district governor David Conn said as a former educator in Papua New Guinea, his objective remains ensuring students are comfortably seated to improve their learning experience.

"Our donation is normally 20 double desks, so that's 40 for a class, that gets a class off the floor onto a desk," Conn said.

"The main thing is just to get every kid in Papua New Guinea off the ground."

Conn said additional requests for desk allocations have been received from several remote and rural schools across the Esa'ala and Samarai-Murua districts.

He said the club hopes to extend similar support to those schools once preliminary logistics and arrangements are finalised.

"We've got requests… obviously we've still got to do Fagalulu if they ever get their act together. We've got requests from Woodlark that we're looking at. We've even had a request from Rossel," Conn said.

item.title: Search continues for Milne Bay dinghy mishap victims
item.description: Search and recovery efforts for seven people missing following a boating incident in the Makamaka local level government [LLG] area of Alotau, Milne Bay, will officially be called off this Friday. It has been almost two weeks since the passenger dinghy encountered trouble on July 23.
item.content:encoded:
Search and recovery efforts for seven people missing following a boating incident in the Makamaka local level government [LLG] area of Alotau, Milne Bay, will officially be called off this Friday.

It has been almost two weeks since the passenger dinghy encountered trouble on July 23.

An additional supply of fuel and rations has been dispatched to assist relatives of the seven missing persons so they can continue search operations until the Friday deadline.

Milne Bay provincial disaster coordinator Randall Ganisi confirmed that the official 72-hour search period under their Standard Operating Procedure [SOP] lapsed on Sunday, forcing official teams to scale down operations.

"We've actually scaled down on the search due to the 72-hour maximum limit on our SOP," Ganisi said.

"We tried to get air assistance, but Milne Bay Province is so limited with air support. We didn't have Jet A-1 fuel to request air support for search."

Ganisi said that to allow for closure, families of the missing individuals requested a final extension of search and recovery efforts until Friday, after which the operation will be formally wound up.

item.title: NYDA rolls out youth strategy in Simbu with three-day socialisation program
item.description: The National Youth Development Authority [NYDA] is currently conducting a three-day socialisation program in Simbu to roll out the National Youth Engagement Strategy [NYES] 2025–2029. The event, scheduled from August 3 to 5, 2026, completed its second day today at Mountain Hut Lodge, where NYDA officials continued presenting the insights and components of the new national framework to provincial,
item.content:encoded:
The National Youth Development Authority [NYDA] is currently conducting a three-day socialisation program in Simbu to roll out the National Youth Engagement Strategy [NYES] 2025–2029.

The event, scheduled from August 3 to 5, 2026, completed its second day today at Mountain Hut Lodge, where NYDA officials continued presenting the insights and components of the new national framework to provincial, district, non-government organisations, church, and other stakeholders.

Acting National Youth Engagement Strategy manager Israel Luluaki said Simbu is the 10th province in the country to involve in the NYES socialisation program.

Luluaki said the 2025–29 strategy is Papua New Guinea’s roadmap for mobilising young people into meaningful structural empowerment and employment.

He said the strategy was formally approved under National Executive Council Decision No. 61/2025, following a Prime Ministerial directive on youth mobilisation issued in January 2024, and will be administered by NYDA under the NYDA Act 2014.

"Key strategic pillars emphasised in the sessions include youth mobilisation and registration, sectoral employment pathways, and the signing of joint inception and implementation plans at provincial and district levels," he said.

The program will culminate on Wednesday and Thursday with the signing of the joint inception and implementation plan by the Simbu provincial government, provincial administrator, and NYDA director general Joe Itaki.

Among the stakeholders present was deputy provincial administrator Kale Simai, who said the socialisation aims to bring young people to the centre of sustainable development through coordinated provincial, district, and stakeholder actions.

item.title: Thousands witness consecration in Buin
item.description: Thousands of faithfuls came from across the Buin Deanery and beyond South Bougainville, to celebrate the consecration of the St. Joseph Husband of Mary Catholic Church at Turiboiru Parish just outside Buin Town over the weekend. The church was packed beyond capacity, overflowing with fatihfuls prayerfully welcoming a modern house of worship, blessed by Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Bougainvill
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of faithfuls came from across the Buin Deanery and beyond South Bougainville, to celebrate the consecration of the St. Joseph Husband of Mary Catholic Church at Turiboiru Parish just outside Buin Town over the weekend.

The church was packed beyond capacity, overflowing with fatihfuls prayerfully welcoming a modern house of worship, blessed by Bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Bougainville Darius Kalusza.

The Bishop said while the church has been blessed to serve as a house of congregation for worship, believers must also renew and rededicate their lives to God.

The blessing and opening of the Turiboiru Church also coincides with the 125th Jubilee Celebration of the Catholic Church in Bougainville.

With the opening of the church, the Parish celebrated its first Thanksgiving mass in line with the Jubilee on Sunday.

On Friday the landing of the first Marist missionaries in Buin in 1903 was re-enacted at Patupatuai Beach, and a procession was led into Turiboiru Parish, marking the start of the Jubilee celebrations.

The event continues onto Pokpok Island and Tubiana Parish in Central Bougainville this weekend and will conclude at the Hahela Parish on Buka Island on August 14.

item.title: Datec outlines Kina-backed expansion plans
item.description: Datec PNG is embarking on a major expansion into new age Information Communication Technology [ICT] services, extending its operations across the country and into the Pacific region. Datec PNG chief executive officer Preetam Talukdar revealed the expansion plans during the launching of the company's new showroom in Lae, Morobe.
item.content:encoded:
Datec PNG is embarking on a major expansion into new age Information Communication Technology [ICT] services, extending its operations across the country and into the Pacific region.

Datec PNG chief executive officer Preetam Talukdar revealed the expansion plans during the launching of the company's new showroom in Lae, Morobe.

Talukdar said Datec PNG remains the largest ICT solutions and service provider in the country, currently employing 250 Papua New Guineans.

"We are decentralising to Mt Hagen, and will extend our services to Honiara (Solomon Islands), and open another commercial building opposite APEC Haus this year," Talukdar said.

"We will then also upgrade our branches in Wewak, Rabaul and Alotau by next year. As we extend to those parts of the country, we are going to increase the number of our employees to 500 by the end of next year."

Talukdar also confirmed that the company plans to establish its own charity foundation to support community initiatives in centers where it operates.

Datec PNG is a subsidiary of state-owned telecommunications provider Telikom PNG. Established in 1986, Datec originally started operations at the Lae Papuan Compound as a subsidiary of Steamships Trading Company before its acquisition by Telikom.

Telikom PNG chairman Shedrick Sendeke assured the people of Lae of the quality, reliability, and relevance of the technology services being offered.

Sendeke said Datec's return to Lae was a homecoming, but on a much larger scale with advanced technological standards designed to keep local businesses and residents connected.

"Returning to Lae is like returning to our origin, so it is not a new location, but on a bigger scale and advanced technology standard service given to the people, so they are not left behind in the newest technology," Sendeke said.

Meanwhile, Talukdar said the official public opening date for the Lae showroom will be announced soon.

Once open, customers in Lae will gain access to the latest IT consumables, consumer electronics, and Artificial Intelligence [AI] integrated products.

item.title: Basil explains K50,000 school project grants
item.description: Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jnr has clarified the funding mechanism behind the construction of a new classroom at Malangta Primary School in Watut, Morobe, following public criticism surrounding the project’s cost and standard. The opening of the building recently drew widespread criticism on social media, with members of the public questioning the overall value and quality of the facility.
item.content:encoded:
Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jnr has clarified the funding mechanism behind the construction of a new classroom at Malangta Primary School in Watut, Morobe, following public criticism surrounding the project’s cost and standard.

The opening of the building recently drew widespread criticism on social media, with members of the public questioning the overall value and quality of the facility.

Speaking in response to the public reaction, Basil said Malangta Primary was among 33 schools across the district that each received a K50,000 grant from the Bulolo District Development Authority [BDDA] to assist with classroom construction.

"The Bulolo Development Authority, as guided by the Bulolo District Development Plan 2023-2027 under infrastructure support, has provided counter funding which is understood to complement funding obtained from the project component of the Government tuition fee subsidy grants," Basil told NBC News.

"The Bulolo Development Authority provided K50,000 in counter funding to 33 schools right across the district, totalling K1,650,000."

Basil said the funding assistance was never meant to cover the total cost of any single building, but was allocated as financial assistance to aid school boards in delivering their own projects, preferably a two-in-one classroom structure.

He said in addition to the cash grants, the BDDA also supplied 100 sheets of roofing iron to each of the 33 recipient schools.

"This support also reduced construction costs and helped schools complete the classroom projects," Basil said.

"Schools were encouraged to source their own timber and contractor, which basically left the school management boards and their administration to take ownership of the funding and deliver an infrastructure project for their school.

"This meant the school management boards and their administration were responsible for deciding how the funds were used, whether to build through community labour, engage carpenters, or award contracts to a contractor. The designs of the classroom projects were also the prerogative of each school."

Basil further clarified that the district administration had no direct involvement in the execution, design, or management of the building works once the funds and roofing sheets were handed over.

According to figures confirmed by the Bulolo District Education Services; five schools have completed, launched, and acquitted their projects, 28 schools have commenced construction and are nearing completion, and, two schools have yet to begin construction.

"The five schools that have completed and launched their classroom project have also fully acquitted for the funding that they have received, and the Office of the Bulolo DDA Chairman and the Bulolo administration are in receipt of the acquittal," Basil said.

He maintained that the BDDA treated every school in the district equally and would not interfere in the internal decisions of local school boards.

"BDDA don’t micromanage. We are not architects or engineers. We have 33 schools, all receive the same," Basil said.

"It’s not always the role of the DDA to do what we did. They should be happy something is better than nothing. There were no special treatment. We treated all 33 schools the same."

item.title: Koroba people told to protect water sources amid El Niño impacts
item.description: The Koroba Lake Kopiago District Development Authority [KLK DDA] is urging communities across the district to protect remaining water sources as severe El Niño conditions take hold, causing widespread water scarcity across the region.
